insight_title: Alaska separates manufacturer clinical submissions from general public comments and enforces a much earlier manufacturer deadline
drug_or_class: All agenda drug classes
why_it_matters: Manufacturers need to engage before the public-comment window; the January 2026 manufacturer deadline was 14 days before the meeting, while general submissions were due two days before the meeting.
evidence_quote_or_summary: For the January 16, 2026 P&T meeting, the notice says manufacturer clinical submissions were accepted until January 2, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. AK time; public materials were requested by January 14, 2026 for inclusion.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 10-22; page marker is Page 1.

insight_title: Alaska directs manufacturers away from committee members and into Prime/NHC-style submission channels
drug_or_class: All PDL products
why_it_matters: Direct committee-member outreach appears discouraged; useful clinical evidence, including off-label peer-reviewed studies, must be packaged through the formal submission form and contractor/state contacts.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The manufacturer form instructs submissions by email to Prime Therapeutics contacts, requests subject line 'Manufacturer Submission,' says P&T members asked that PDL comments go directly to Prime, and requests no direct member contact. It also frames the form as a request for peer-reviewed literature, including off-label peer-reviewed studies.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 10-21; page marker and embedded form page both indicate Page 1.

insight_title: Arizona tells manufacturers exactly which reviewed classes need rebate offers and which do not
therapeutic_area: Cross-therapeutic; HAE, LHRH, new drugs, SGLT2, oncology, PAH, ulcerative colitis
drug_or_class: Hereditary angioedema treatments; new drugs; pituitary suppressive agents/LHRH; multiple no-offer classes
why_it_matters: The manufacturer letter is a forward-looking rebate and class-review map: it distinguishes categories where supplemental rebate economics are active from classes under review without current rebate offers.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The January 2026 letter states supplemental rebate offers were not requested for classes including SGLT2s, oncology oral-hematologic, PAH agents, and ulcerative colitis, while offers were requested for HAE treatments, seven named new drugs, and LHRH agents.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 14-40 and 82-98; page marker changes to Page 2 at line 79.

insight_title: Spravato was recommended preferred in Arizona's January 2026 antidepressant review with no grandfathering
drug_or_class: Spravato (esketamine); antidepressants, other
why_it_matters: For treatment-resistant depression strategy, Spravato appears on the recommended preferred list, but the slide flags no grandfathering, so implementation details and PA criteria still matter.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The recommendation slides list Spravato nasal under preferred products for Antidepressants, Other and mark Grandfathering as No.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 34-58; page marker is Page 4.

insight_title: Arizona's LHRH recommendations preferred Fensolvi while grandfathering selected Lupron Depot pediatric/6-month products
drug_or_class: Pituitary suppressive agents, LHRH; Fensolvi; Lupron Depot
why_it_matters: The state can prefer a new or specific LHRH option while explicitly protecting selected existing patients; market-share impact may depend on new starts versus grandfathered lives.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The January 2026 recommendation slides list Fensolvi 6-month, Lupron Depot 1-month, and Lupron Depot-Ped 1-month as preferred, with grandfathering for Lupron-Depot Ped 3 Months, Lupron-Depot Ped 6 Months, and Lupron-Depot 6 Months.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 515-526; page marker is Page 36.

insight_title: Arkansas splits clinical review from a closed net-cost review committee
drug_or_class: All PDL classes under review
why_it_matters: Public clinical rationale is only part of the access decision. Preferred status can depend on a separate closed review of state and federal rebates and final net cost.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The PDL overview describes SSR offers, GNUP terms, a public Drug Review Committee for CER/safety/efficacy, and a closed Drug Cost Committee that reviews proprietary rebate/net-cost data before final preferred-status recommendations.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 7-17, 24-39, and 43-52; page marker changes at line 42.

insight_title: Arkansas gives a 30-day implementation runway for moves to non-preferred status, but preferred moves may occur faster
drug_or_class: Medications moving to non-preferred status
why_it_matters: A brand moving to non-preferred status has a defined monitoring window for provider notices, claim messages, patient-specific prescriber outreach where feasible, and emergency-supply planning.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The PDL overview says changes moving a drug to non-preferred status are communicated at least 30 days before implementation, claims can generate future-change messages, and emergency dispensing may cover up to a five-day supply; drugs moving to preferred status without specific PA criteria may change sooner.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 53-69 and 76-86; page marker is Page 2.

insight_title: Adult stimulant access is tied to functional impairment in school, work, or job-seeking, not just diagnosis
drug_or_class: C-II stimulants; Qelbree; atomoxetine; clonidine IR; guanfacine IR
why_it_matters: Adult ADHD access barriers include documentation of DSM-V symptoms, employment/school impairment, and medical necessity if neither employed nor enrolled; Qelbree is further disadvantaged against atomoxetine and preferred C-II stimulants.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The form says atomoxetine, clonidine IR, and guanfacine IR do not require PA for adult ADHD; Qelbree is non-preferred and requires medical necessity over atomoxetine and preferred C-II stimulants. The form asks about school, employment, job-seeking, and limits some job-seeking treatment support to three months.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 15-17 and 76-119; relevant functional questions are on Page 2.

insight_title: Xolair asthma approval requires six months of controller-medication compliance, while IgE is not a renewal hurdle
drug_or_class: Xolair (omalizumab)
why_it_matters: For biologic asthma access, Arkansas uses claims/chart evidence of standard controller adherence as a gate, but it avoids forcing repeat IgE evidence at renewal.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The Xolair form requires at least six consecutive months of compliance with daily standard controller medications and states the Medicaid drug profile will be reviewed; it also says IgE levels are not applicable for PA renewal requests.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 38-51 and 102-106; controller-compliance requirement begins on Page 1 and IgE note appears on Page 2.

insight_title: Connecticut has statutory PA safety valves: 14-day emergency supply, 24-hour deemed approval, mental-health continuity, and antiretroviral PDL exclusion
drug_or_class: Non-preferred drugs; mental-health drugs; antiretrovirals
why_it_matters: State law can blunt access restrictions even where a drug is non-preferred; mental-health and antiretroviral products have special protections that should be separated from ordinary PDL logic.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The State Law Requirements document says pharmacists dispense a one-time 14-day supply when prescriber authorization cannot be obtained, PA requests not granted or denied within 24 hours are deemed granted, prior authorization is not required for mental-health-related drugs filled/refilled at least once in the prior year, and antiretroviral classes are not included on PDLs.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 17-34; PDF extraction lacks explicit page marker, but all cited text is on the first extracted page.

insight_title: Connecticut Medicaid step therapy is statutorily capped at one preferred-drug failure and excludes mental-health drugs
drug_or_class: Step therapy categories
why_it_matters: Manufacturers can use the statutory limit to challenge over-sequenced criteria: step therapy cannot require multiple preferred failures and must offer expedited overrides for medical necessity or expected harm.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The State Law Requirements document says step therapy may require trying and failing only one preferred-list drug, does not apply to mental-health-related drugs, and must provide an expedited override when the preferred treatment failed, is expected to be ineffective, likely causes harm, or medical necessity supports the requested drug.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 37-57; PDF extraction lacks explicit page marker, but all cited text is on the first extracted page.

insight_title: Connecticut's 2026 TNF criteria prefer selected adalimumab and infliximab products but preserve medical exceptions for destabilization and indication mismatch
drug_or_class: TNF inhibitors; adalimumab, infliximab, etanercept, certolizumab, golimumab
why_it_matters: Biosimilar and originator positioning is product-specific. Non-preferred adalimumab/infliximab can still clear PA with failure/ADE to preferred formulations or medical reasons such as age, weight, indication, or destabilization risk.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The TNF criteria list preferred adalimumab-adaz, Hadlima, Humira, Enbrel, and infliximab with implementation date 1/1/2026. Non-preferred adalimumab and infliximab requests require trial/failure or ADE/ADR to preferred formulations, and other non-preferred TNF requests require a medical reason the preferred TNF cannot be used.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 14-44 and 404-485; detailed criteria are on Page 3.

insight_title: Connecticut's topical antipsoriatic rules make samples unusable as step-therapy proof and require recent preferred-class trials
drug_or_class: Topical antipsoriatics; Zoryve 0.3% cream; calcipotriene/calcitriol products
why_it_matters: Commercial sampling may not help patients meet Medicaid criteria; documentation must show claims or chart-note evidence of preferred therapy, and formulation-level preferences can override brand/generic assumptions.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The criteria state samples do not meet step therapy or continuation requirements, prior therapies are verified through claims/chart notes, brand-vs-generic exceptions need documented medical reasons, and Zoryve cream requires plaque psoriasis plus trial/failure of one preferred topical vitamin D analog or topical corticosteroid within the previous six months.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 125-153 and 167-172; main criteria begin on Page 2.

insight_title: Connecticut explicitly uses cost-effectiveness to set CAPS PDL status when clinical preference is not generalizable
drug_or_class: CAPS agents; Kineret, Ilaris, Arcalyst
why_it_matters: For rare-disease classes with limited head-to-head evidence, the state's own rationale says clinical differentiation may not drive preference; cost-effective positioning can become decisive.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The CAPS criteria say AAAAI does not specify one agent over another, choice should be individualized, preference cannot be generalized, and PDL status may remain with the most cost-effective agents.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 42-60 and 131-147; cost-effectiveness rationale is on Page 2.

insight_title: Florida's December 2025 P&T changes show new products defaulting to Non-PDL, with one Non-CF bronchiectasis exception carrying clinical PA
therapeutic_area: Cross-therapeutic; immunology, endocrinology, rare disease, pulmonary
drug_or_class: Imuldosa, Leqselvi, Brynovin, Kirsty, Anzupgo, Brinsupri and other new products
why_it_matters: The access impact appears in the post-meeting change summary, not just the agenda: several newly reviewed products were assigned Non-PDL status, while Brinsupri was assigned PDL with clinical PA effective April 1, 2026.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The Florida summary is from the December 12, 2025 P&T meeting and says changes are effective April 1, 2026. It lists multiple new drugs as Non-PDL and lists Brinsupri for non-CF bronchiectasis as PDL with a clinical PA comment.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 2-4, 64-78, 108-142, and 184-191; page marker embedded in header indicates Page 1.

insight_title: Florida's GLP-1 access barriers are embedded as age, days-supply, volume, and starter-fill edits rather than plain PA status
drug_or_class: Mounjaro, Ozempic, Rybelsus, Trulicity, Victoza, Saxenda
why_it_matters: Even when PA status must be checked separately, utilization edits can constrain titration, starter dosing, and refill cadence for high-budget incretin products.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The limitations file states it may or may not indicate PA status, then lists product-level edits: Mounjaro minimum age 10 and max 2 mL every 30 days; Ozempic minimum age 18 with dose-pen day-supply/volume limits; Rybelsus 3 mg limited to 30 tablets every 365 days; Trulicity and Victoza have age/volume limits.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 7-10, 3722-3724, 4226-4234, 5098-5102, 6065-6067, and 6332-6334; Mounjaro appears on Page 63, with related products on later pages.

insight_title: Georgia's October 2024 DURB pushed several new drugs to NP/PA after clinical and financial evaluation, including Rezdiffra for MASH
therapeutic_area: MASH/NASH; rare disease; gastroenterology; ophthalmology; nephrology
drug_or_class: Rezdiffra, Agamree, Voquezna, Xdemvy, Xphozah
why_it_matters: Georgia's new-drug pathway can convert high-profile launches into non-preferred/prior-authorized access shortly after review; Rezdiffra's MASH placement is a notable metabolic-liver signal.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The DURB minutes say the Board made recommendations after clinical and financial evaluations. Attachment material shows Agamree, Rezdiffra, Voquezna, Xdemvy, and Xphozah recommended NP/PA, and the listed Georgia FFS Medicaid/PeachCare changes are effective January 1, 2025.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 361-365 and 668-696; implementation list is on Page 10.

insight_title: Georgia generally waits six months post-market before DURB new-drug review, then allows a narrow manufacturer appeal window after quarterly meetings
drug_or_class: New drugs and supplemental rebate classes
why_it_matters: Launch teams should not only watch meeting dates; Georgia exposes a pre-meeting forum, a roughly 30-day posting window, and a 10-business-day post-meeting appeal channel to GDCH before final decisions settle.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The Georgia handout says new entities are generally not reviewed until on the market at least six months, drugs/classes under review are posted approximately 30 days before the Manufacturers' Forum, DURB recommendations go to GDCH for final decisions, and manufacturers may request an appeal meeting within 10 business days after each quarterly DURB meeting.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 749-802; page marker is Page 11.

insight_title: California's DUR alerts include opioid-specific early-refill sensitivity and a four-prescription additive-toxicity trigger for CNS-depressant classes
drug_or_class: Opioids, benzodiazepines, skeletal muscle relaxants, sleep drugs/tranquilizers, antipsychotics, selected psychotropics
why_it_matters: DUR friction may arise before PA: claims can surface safety alerts based on refill interval, therapeutic duplication, additive toxicity, and alert-priority hierarchy.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The DUR JSON lists active alerts including early refill where refill interval is less than 75% of previous day supply and less than 90% for opioids. It also lists additive toxicity when a target drug exceeds a threshold of four or more active prescriptions across opioid pain/cough, benzodiazepine, muscle relaxant, sleep/tranquilizer, antipsychotic, and selected psychotropic CNS-depressant categories.
validation_note: Verified against local JSON text line 11; source is JSON/HTML-like content, so page number is null.

insight_title: Alabama's prescription-limit policy exempts several sensitive classes but caps many adults at five drugs per month
drug_or_class: Adult outpatient prescriptions; antipsychotics; HIV drugs; seizure drugs
why_it_matters: Access issues may appear as benefit-limit friction rather than PDL status: adult polypharmacy can hit monthly caps, while selected classes have explicit exemptions.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The Alabama prescription-limits page says adults are usually limited to five drugs per month, four of which may be brand drugs; three-month maintenance supply drugs do not count; children and nursing-home patients are exempt; antipsychotic, HIV, and seizure drugs are also exempt.
validation_note: Verified by local text search around the prescription-limits body; source is HTML, so page number is null.
